newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Oct trade surplus falls to C$1.49 bln.
newsitem.headline: Canada Oct trade surplus falls to C$1.49 bln.

text.p: Canada's merchandise trade surplus narrowed in October to C$1.49 billion from C$3.26 billion in September (revised from C$3.23 billion), Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Note: Figures in billions of current Canadian dollars, on a balance of payments basis, seasonally adjusted.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.97 billion in October. The survey also forecast imports of C$20.02 billion and exports of C$22.86 billion in October.

Statistics Canada said declines in exports in October were widespread, but the largest decline was in shipments of automotive products, due to a three-week strike at General Motors Corp's Canadian unit.

Shipments to the United States, the primary destination for Canadian vehicle exports, fell 10.8 percent in October. Shipments to Japan and the European Union declined as well while shipments to all other trading partners rose.
The strike at General Motors also affected imports, which dropped 3.3 percent in October, due to lower automotive parts imports and fewer purchases of machinery and equipment.
Imports from the United States fell 7.0 percent in the month but shipments from all other trading partners rose.
